headline: Launch an AI Agent that automates multi‑step research workflows and showcase it worldwide to boost your AI engineer portfolio.
why_now: Signal scores above 90 on GitHub, Hugging Face, and news coverage prove a surge in agentic tooling and hiring demand. Companies are racing to embed AI agents in products, so a visible demo now translates directly into job offers and freelance gigs.
study: Read the LangChain and AutoGPT docs; run the official notebooks to grasp agent scaffolding.
Complete a hands‑on tutorial building a tool‑using agent (e.g., web‑search + PDF summarizer) on a sandbox repo.
Study API‑integration patterns (REST, GraphQL) and security best practices for agents that call external services.
Explore prompt‑engineering for planning and tool selection; experiment with few‑shot prompting in OpenAI or Anthropic models.
Review open‑source agent ecosystems (CrewAI, AgentVerse) to understand modular design and community standards.

build.title: Research‑Assistant AI Agent for Academic Literature
build.description: An autonomous agent that takes a research question, searches arXiv, fetches PDFs, extracts key findings, and generates a concise literature‑review summary. It demonstrates end‑to‑end planning, tool use (search API, PDF parser, LLM summarizer), and multi‑step reasoning—exactly what employers are hunting for.
deliverables: GitHub repo with clean README, CI workflow, and unit tests
Live demo hosted on Render or Railway with a simple web UI
Technical write‑up (blog post or Medium article) explaining architecture, prompts, and lessons learned

publish: Post the repo link with a short demo video on the #ai-agents channel of the LangChain Discord and on the Hugging Face Spaces community.
Write a 1500‑word article on Medium, cross‑post to dev.to, and tag #AI‑Agents, #LangChain, #ResearchAssistant.
Share the project on LinkedIn tagging relevant AI product leads and include a carousel of screenshots and performance metrics.
Submit a concise project summary to the weekly AI‑Engineer newsletter (e.g., AI Engineer Weekly) and to the “Awesome AI Agents” GitHub list.
skills: Prompt engineering for planning & tool selection
Designing and orchestrating multi‑step AI workflows
Deploying LLM‑backed services with FastAPI and Docker
Version control, CI/CD, and reproducible environments
Performance evaluation and error handling of agents
risks: API rate limits or cost spikes when scaling the agent; mitigate with caching and usage monitoring.
Prompt brittleness – the agent may fail on ambiguous queries; address with robust fallback logic and extensive testing.
Keeping up with rapid changes in agent frameworks; allocate time for periodic library updates.
confidence: High confidence – the signals, tooling maturity, and market demand strongly support this concrete portfolio project.
